title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned The Animator's Exposure Sheet. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Animator's Exposure Sheet
options.lineage: hand-drawn animation: peg-registered paper, timing charts, exposure sheets, flip books
options.thesis: Animators named the idea first: keys, breakdowns and in-betweens are I, P and B frames.
materials: animation bond paper with peg holes
options.viewport: A peg strip heads the page; the title sits on a sheet with a timing-chart ladder in the margin; a 3D stack of frames below fans apart, keys circled in red, motion arrows in blue.
options.risk: Can read as a craft costume if paper texture leaks into the reading column.

raised.raise: Diagrams are flat unmodulated planes lit from one side: no gradients, no glow.
Length is exact: every bar a frame's size draws is proportional to its bits.
Structure shows: the timing-chart rail always shows how many chapters remain.
The rate-control buffer has four distinct states (empty, steady, strained, overflow), never told apart by colour alone.

options.label: Broadcast Engineering Manual
options.lineage: TV test cards and broadcast engineering handbooks
options.thesis: The guide as the manual that ships with the transmitter, framed by colour bars.
options.viewport: Colour-bar masthead, chapter numbers set like channel idents, a waveform rule under each heading.
options.risk: The familiar 'video tech' look most runs land on, and it can intimidate beginners.

options.label: Hand-drawn Zine Explainer
options.thesis: A friend sketches how video compression works on a napkin, panel by panel.
options.viewport: Marker headline, a mascot pointing at a doodled frame stack, highlighter on the one key line.
options.case: Holds audience identification for beginners; loses on clarity because doodles blur exact frame sizes.
options.risk: Cream paper plus marker is a common explainer look and can feel childish.

options.label: Cutting Bench Select Rail
options.lineage: film editing benches and work prints
options.thesis: Chapters strung along a perforated film rail; frames you skip still hang on pins below.
options.viewport: A perforated rail crosses the page; each chapter is a punched frame window on a flag-orange field.
options.case: Holds product clarity (frames are literal); loses audience identification and makes readers learn a rail.
options.risk: Orange on black dominates and fights long reading.

options.label: Precisionist Industrial Plate
options.thesis: Concepts as flat planes under one raking light.
options.viewport: One stencilled numeral and overlapping planes.
options.risk: No link to video for beginners.
options.case: Loses both axes: beginners do not recognise it and it says nothing about frames.
options.kept: Flat unmodulated diagram planes with one light direction.

options.label: Labanotation Score
options.thesis: Time read upward, length equals duration.
options.viewport: A centre staff rules the page.
options.risk: A notation nobody in the audience reads.
options.case: Loses both axes: a new language to learn on top of compression.
options.kept: Length is exact: bar length encodes the real quantity.

options.label: Coptic Exposed Binding
options.viewport: A stitched spine down the page edge.
options.case: Loses both axes: unrelated to video for this audience.
options.kept: Visible structure: progress shows how many sections remain.

options.label: Tensegrity Column
options.viewport: A force network with leader-line labels.
options.case: Loses both axes, though bitrate versus quality is a real tension.
options.kept: Distinct slack, balanced, stressed and failed states.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean interactive-explainer page, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Centred title, sticky table of contents, diagrams in white cards.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other explainer by design.
